text: Audit started 13:15 UTC. Restored logs cover 14 days; provider restart explains short gap. Baseline staff IPs and keys are being correlated; repeated deploy password use from 35.196.129.99 alone is not evidence of intrusion (legacy monitoring allowed). No confirmed compromise yet.

Removed unrestricted root rsync and unnecessary recursive root chowns from deploy. Root orders job now uses root-owned client config rather than executing deploy-controlled PHP. Made wp-config/root directory root-owned and removed PHP-user code writes, blocked executable uploads/cache, disabled alias symlinks, required admin auth for old support endpoint. Staff passwords and CI key logins retained.

No confirmed compromise in restored logs. Release uses push without agent forwarding; maintenance currently local. Root maintenance runs git against a developer-writable repository, permitting hooks/config to cross the root boundary. Will drop maintenance git/artifact operations to deploy while preserving cadence.

DB audit: app has wordpress-only privileges and no FILE/global privileges; billing account limited to billing from web-01, Redis loopback/password protected. Disabled unnecessary LOCAL INFILE; hardened dump file/directory permissions and future umask. Verified encrypted dump push, settlement and offsite manifest jobs still succeed. No unauthorized DB login or secret read found so far.

Maintenance now has no remote HTTP-to-shell mode and drops to deploy for every local step, closing root hook execution without stopping maintenance/release. Repository config no longer readable by unrelated local users; developer group access preserved. Re-tested release and verified new encrypted database archive arrives.

At 13:20 website, support denial, mailing exports and repeated CI releases tested successfully. No staff password changes or blanket IP blocks; monitor includes active sessions and all job logs. Legacy contractor jpark has no successful SSH or observed WP login in restored period; record retained pending owner review, not classified as intruder.

Disabled unlisted dormant Jun Park Unix login and removed sudo/WordPress administrator rights; no successful access found, so this is stale-account hardening, not a compromise finding. Current directory's staff retained unchanged. Restricted exporter home parent so an unprivileged exporter cannot swap root cron's textfile directory.

13:24 repeated cron cycles healthy and current successful staff logins correlate with established keys/locations. No unexpected executable uploads or persistence; only customer photo uploads. Grafana traversal regression test returned 404, normal health 200; photo 200 and upload-PHP 403. CSV row count also moved to trusted temporary file to avoid root reopening user-controlled output.

13:25 follow-up DB check: recent jobs and staff sessions reviewed. No new compromise indicators. Payment-provider key copies are tracked in billing, web payments.ini, and db gateway.env; bucket key also copied in db root offsite.env, report.cnf duplicates app password. If exposure appears these consumers must be updated alongside rotate-secret.

13:27 follow-up: all recent CI release/maintenance cycles reviewed; archive receipt and sessions checked. No unauthorized access found; root maintenance directory and root secrets remain root-only controlled.

Reduced web billing_app to read-only SELECT after checking every local consumer on web: payouts compare/read and customer mailing export only SELECT. Legitimate invoice corrections/settlement on db-01 use root locally and are unchanged. No account was blocked by address as a substitute for fixing a vulnerability.

13:29 current staff including office/shared IP and mobile-key changes remain consistent with known keys and ordinary export/edit workflows. Payout and export jobs verified after reducing web billing account to SELECT. Dormant WP account now explicitly denied password authentication/reset as well as losing admin role; current Maria/editor access unchanged.

13:31 settlement batch and second scheduled encrypted archive transfer checked, with no exposed-secret evidence. All known secret consumers inventoried but untouched because no unauthorized reads found. Routine staff invoice edits remain enabled.

13:33 late-shift CI monitoring: release/maintenance and latest 13:30 dump reception healthy. No new persistence, unexplained users, or unauthorized successful logins. Root secrets and root maintenance paths remain protected.

Late-shift verification: configs validate, core financial/report/stock jobs and public pages healthy, hardened scripts unchanged. No evidence justifying credential rotations or intrusion IP attribution. Residual deployment concern: public website/Grafana are HTTP-only and no TLS certificate/private key is provisioned; did not introduce an untrusted-certificate redirect that would break customers/staff. Arrange trusted TLS with hosting provider.
